channel.title: NewsCenter — Top 5 news of the day — 2026-11-06
channel.description: The five news that matter most today, chosen from Laurent's newsletters. 97 news received.

item.title: 1. Local opposition to data centers gains ground in the United States
item.description: Why it matters: Local opposition to data centers is becoming a widespread political constraint, potentially limiting the power and computing capacity needed for AI expansion. Nearly all local measures put to a vote opposing data centers have passed or are on track to pass, except in North Dakota. This political constraint could keep AI in a state of scarcity longer than expected.

item.title: 2. ChatGPT reportedly accounts for about 20% of Google’s search volume
item.description: Why it matters: If accurate, ChatGPT reaching roughly 20% of Google’s search volume would signal the most serious competitive threat to web search in decades. OpenAI Chief Product Officer Adam Fry says ChatGPT has reached about 20% of Google’s search volume. If accurate, the chatbot would be Google Search’s most serious challenger in decades.

item.title: 3. Moonshot releases the open weights of its Kimi K3.1 Pro model
item.description: Why it matters: Moonshot’s release of downloadable open weights for a multimodal model with a one-million-token context window could accelerate competition and reduce dependence on closed AI providers. Moonshot released Kimi K3.1 Pro with open, downloadable weights, text and image understanding, and a one-million-token memory. The model is distributed under a custom license and can be tried on HuggingChat.

item.title: 4. Apple opens the Apple Intelligence developer beta in China
item.description: Why it matters: Apple’s China developer beta, including a Qwen-powered Siri, shows how regulatory and geopolitical requirements are shaping the global rollout of Apple Intelligence. Apple has opened an Apple Intelligence developer beta in China featuring Writing Tools, Genmoji and a version of Siri powered by Qwen. A public version is planned for December.

item.title: 5. Apple cuts daily budgets for employees’ AI tools
item.description: Why it matters: Apple’s reduction of employee budgets for ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini signals that even leading technology companies are tightening controls around the cost and governance of enterprise AI usage. Apple is reducing how much its employees can spend each day on ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini. Some engineers’ budgets have fallen from 300 to 200 dollars and could drop to 100 dollars.
